classification_reason: A useful descriptive word for skillful planning that often involves deception, with an important contrast against sly and neutral clever.

senses.definition: Clever at planning how to achieve something, especially through deception or by hiding your intentions.
senses.example: The con artist used a cunning scheme to gain their trust.
senses.usage_note: Cunning emphasizes skillful planning, while sly emphasizes secrecy or concealed intentions and clever is normally neutral.

synonyms.note: neutral and does not imply deception

senses.definition: Skill in achieving something through clever planning or deception.
senses.example: The general relied on cunning rather than brute force.
senses.usage_note: The noun is uncountable and is more common in literary or formal writing.
